description:
The native runtime-test emitter turns the module's named structs into a chain of schema-id compares by iterating a HashMap. runtime_test.rs emit_named_struct_axis reads e.named_schema_ids().values() for all_named, and emit_arity_set_membership reads the same map for its cofinite 'not a named schema' half. Rust's default HashMap hasher is seeded per process, so the order of the emitted icmp/bor chain is not a function of the module: two compilations of the same source can emit the same question as different instruction sequences.

The answer is unaffected -- it is an OR over equality compares, so any order decides the same values -- which is why nothing has caught it. What it costs is comparability: a byte-identical comparison of two BackendPrograms or of emitted code across runs cannot distinguish 'the compiler made a different decision' from 'the hasher handed back a different order'.

Pre-existing; fz-wof moved the reading into emit_arity_set_membership without changing it. The fix is an ordered source for the set -- the same module-scoped table fz-gee.11 wants for the interpreter's side of it, so the two are worth settling together even though the invariants differ: fz-gee.11 is about work proportional to the question, this one about emission being a function of the input.
title: Emitted named-schema compares follow HashMap order, so the same module can emit different IR
